# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, us…

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, us…

One test change raises a flag: `test/cli/agent_hub_overlay_guard_test.dart` was weakened — the assertion `isNot(contains('scout#1'))` was changed to `isNot(contains('scout#1 (explore)'))`. The reason is legitimate (the status row legitimately paints `run scout#1` in the chat view), but wait — let me think about this. The hub overlay guard test verifies that overlay content doesn't leak into the chat view. The new status row legitimately shows the subagent name in the chat view — that's by design (gh-1415). So the test needed to anchor on the full tree row form. That's reasonable, though weakening the assertion from name → name (type) does reduce the guard's sensitivity. The new subagent board shows the name so it's not a leak. OK.

Now the key files to review:
1. `subagent_board.dart` — reviewed above. Potential issues:
   - `subagentRecordOf` — previewSource uses `task ?? handle.task`. Check `SubagentHandle` for the `task` field.
   - `subagentAgeLabel`: `2h15` format — `'${hours}h${(minutes % 60).toString().padLeft(2, '0')}m'` — wait, `2h15m` is 5 cells > 4! Let me check: hours=2, minutes%60=15 → "2h15m" — that's 5 characters. The doc comment says "Fixed ≤ 4 cells: `42s`, `12m`, `2h15`, capped at `99h+`" — but the code produces `2h15m` (5 cells), not `2h15` (4 cells). Hmm — wait let me re-read:

```dart
  return '${hours}h${(minutes % 60).toString().padLeft(2, '0')}m';
```

For 2h15m → `2h15m` — that's 5 chars. The doc says ≤ 4 cells and gives example `2h15`. So the code contradicts the doc comment. Also `10h05m` = 6 cells! And since `age` is `padLeft(_ageCells)` = padLeft(4), a 5-6 cell value would break the fixed width and reflow the row (misaligning neighbors). Actually the age field is just joined into head: `'$glyph $state $name $age $cost'` — if age is 5-6 cells, head grows and the total width computation may overflow `w`. Let me check: `nameBudget = (w - (_railFloorCells - 1)).clamp(1, _nameCells)` and `previewBudget = w - _railFloorCells - nameBudget`. If w = 100: railFloor = 2+1+4+1+1+1+4+1+4 = let me compute: `_glyphZoneCells + 1 + _stateCells + 1 + 1 + 1 + _ageCells + 1 + _costCells` = 2+1+4+1+1+1+4+1+4 = 19. nameBudget = (100 - 18).clamp(1,16) = 16. previewBudget = 100 - 19 - 16 = 65. head = 2 +1+ 4 +1+ 16 +1+ 4 +1+ 4 = 34 cells; head + 1 + 65 = 100. OK.

But if age renders 5-6 cells (e.g. `2h15m`), head = 35-36 and total = 101-102 > width → line wraps or overflows the budget. The TUI painter clips `_clipToWidth(boardRow.text)` — so the preview would get clipped, but the row's own fixed-rail would be misaligned vs other rows (age column not fixed width). Minor issue but a real bug vs its own spec ("Fixed ≤ 4 cells", "digit growth never reflows the row"). Also `padLeft(4)` on `99h+` (4 cells) is fine. So the bug: hours < 60 & minutes%60 → `XhYYm` is 5+ cells for hours 1-99 (e.g. `1h05m` = 5 cells, `12h34m` = 6 cells). Doc comment says the format is `2h15`. So there's an inconsistency — the trailing `m` makes it 5 cells minimum for hours≥1. This is a genuine bug (BLOCKING? It's a display misalignment for agents running ≥1h; the row exceeds width → wrap/clip). Severity: the code contradicts its own documented invariant (AC1: exactly ONE line ≤ 100 columns; E1: fixed rail). For a row at width 100 with a long preview, the extra 2 cells push the line to 102 > 100 → wrap (violates "never wrap"). I'd class as BLOCKING? Hmm. Let me think — is it a "broken behavior" bug? For subagents running over an hour, rows misalign and can wrap. The card's whole point is alignment/density. It's an edge (age ≥ 1h subagent) but the pin facts mention 12m/41k in the example. The unit tests presumably test `2h15m`? Let me check the test file to see what golden strings they assert.

Let me also verify the claimed AC1 "≤ 100 columns" test.

2. `TaskBoardRegion.upsert`: `existing.settledAt = null` for non-terminal — resume revives the row. But wait: if a child is re-spawned... ids are unique so unlikely.

Interesting: in `upsert`, `_pruneSettled()` is only called on the existing-row path — not when a new row is inserted (inserts are non-terminal, so no pruning needed... actually pruning settled rows only matters when count > cap, and a new insert can't add a settled row. Fine).

But there's a subtle issue: `rows()` dedups names across the VISIBLE set — comment says "a folded row cannot force a suffix on a visible one" — the code counts `_rows.values` which IS the visible set (folded rows are removed). OK consistent.

3. Coordinator: `refresh()` iterates `handles` and upserts each. But rows for subagents that are removed from the registry: `handles` — does the registry retain completed subagents forever (retained subagents)? The description says "retained `SubagentHandle` registry". If a handle is removed from the registry (e.g. after abort/retire), the region row would remain forever (region never removes rows except via `_pruneSettled` cap and `clear()`). Terminal rows persist until 4-cap fold. That's per spec (persist one line, fold on pressure). But a row whose handle is evicted would keep ticking? No — terminal rows don't tick (`hasLive` only live rows). But their age would freeze? Age keeps recomputing from spawnedAt — wait, `rows(now:)` recomputes age for terminal rows too! So a settled row's age keeps growing every render... but the coordinator's `_push` dedupe only pushes when text changes — the age of a settled row changes only when the minute flips (minute granularity). So a done row's age ticks up indefinitely (12m → 13m...) — is that intended? The spec says the row collapses to a one-liner summary; an age that keeps ticking on a done row is arguably fine (age of the agent lifetime) — omp keeps elapsed time. That's fine-ish.

Actually wait — there's a subtle dedupe issue: after the last live row settles, the flash period is 3s. Let me trace: coordinator `_push()` computes rows with `bright` flags; dedupe on texts; if texts unchanged, no push. So after a settle at t0: refresh() pushes rows with bright=true (inside flash). Flash end at +3s: nothing re-renders → row remains bright indefinitely. The PTY E2E asserts `done\s+boardwatch` appears — it would pass even if bright. blocks.text:
Interesting. One test change raises a flag: `test/cli/agent_hub_overlay_guard_test.dart` was weakened — the assertion `isNot(contains('scout#1'))` was changed to `isNot(contains('scout#1 (explore)'))`. The reason is legitimate (the status row legitimately paints `run scout#1` in the chat view), but wait — let me think about this. The hub overlay guard test verifies that overlay content doesn't leak into the chat view. The new status row legitimately shows the subagent name in the chat view — that's by design (gh-1415). So the test needed to anchor on the full tree row form. That's reasonable, though weakening the assertion from name → name (type) does reduce the guard's sensitivity. The new subagent board shows the name so it's not a leak. OK.

Now the key files to review:
1. `subagent_board.dart` — reviewed above. Potential issues:
   - `subagentRecordOf` — previewSource uses `task ?? handle.task`. Check `SubagentHandle` for the `task` field.
   - `subagentAgeLabel`: `2h15` format — `'${hours}h${(minutes % 60).toString().padLeft(2, '0')}m'` — wait, `2h15m` is 5 cells > 4! Let me check: hours=2, minutes%60=15 → "2h15m" — that's 5 characters. The doc comment says "Fixed ≤ 4 cells: `42s`, `12m`, `2h15`, capped at `99h+`" — but the code produces `2h15m` (5 cells), not `2h15` (4 cells). Hmm — wait let me re-read:

```dart
  return '${hours}h${(minutes % 60).toString().padLeft(2, '0')}m';
```

For 2h15m → `2h15m` — that's 5 chars. The doc says ≤ 4 cells and gives example `2h15`. So the code contradicts the doc comment. Also `10h05m` = 6 cells! And since `age` is `padLeft(_ageCells)` = padLeft(4), a 5-6 cell value would break the fixed width and reflow the row (misaligning neighbors). Actually the age field is just joined into head: `'$glyph $state $name $age $cost'` — if age is 5-6 cells, head grows and the total width computation may overflow `w`. Let me check: `nameBudget = (w - (_railFloorCells - 1)).clamp(1, _nameCells)` and `previewBudget = w - _railFloorCells - nameBudget`. If w = 100: railFloor = 2+1+4+1+1+1+4+1+4 = let me compute: `_glyphZoneCells + 1 + _stateCells + 1 + 1 + 1 + _ageCells + 1 + _costCells` = 2+1+4+1+1+1+4+1+4 = 19. nameBudget = (100 - 18).clamp(1,16) = 16. previewBudget = 100 - 19 - 16 = 65. head = 2 +1+ 4 +1+ 16 +1+ 4 +1+ 4 = 34 cells; head + 1 + 65 = 100. OK.

But if age renders 5-6 cells (e.g. `2h15m`), head = 35-36 and total = 101-102 > width → line wraps or overflows the budget. The TUI painter clips `_clipToWidth(boardRow.text)` — so the preview would get clipped, but the row's own fixed-rail would be misaligned vs other rows (age column not fixed width). Minor issue but a real bug vs its own spec ("Fixed ≤ 4 cells", "digit growth never reflows the row"). Also `padLeft(4)` on `99h+` (4 cells) is fine. So the bug: hours < 60 & minutes%60 → `XhYYm` is 5+ cells for hours 1-99 (e.g. `1h05m` = 5 cells, `12h34m` = 6 cells). Doc comment says the format is `2h15`. So there's an inconsistency — the trailing `m` makes it 5 cells minimum for hours≥1. This is a genuine bug (BLOCKING? It's a display misalignment for agents running ≥1h; the row exceeds width → wrap/clip). Severity: the code contradicts its own documented invariant (AC1: exactly ONE line ≤ 100 columns; E1: fixed rail). For a row at width 100 with a long preview, the extra 2 cells push the line to 102 > 100 → wrap (violates "never wrap"). I'd class as BLOCKING? Hmm. Let me think — is it a "broken behavior" bug? For subagents running over an hour, rows misalign and can wrap. The card's whole point is alignment/density. It's an edge (age ≥ 1h subagent) but the pin facts mention 12m/41k in the example. The unit tests presumably test `2h15m`? Let me check the test file to see what golden strings they assert.

Let me also verify the claimed AC1 "≤ 100 columns" test.

🚨 **BLOCKING: the settle flash never collapses to dim in the pushed TUI (delta 9 / AC3)**

`_push()` dedupes on **text only**, and the 1 Hz ticker disarms as soon as no row is live — so the post-flash render (`bright=false`, 3 s after settle) is never delivered to the TUI.

Flow: settle event → `refresh()` → `upsert` stamps `settledAt` → `_push()` ships rows with `bright=true` (inside the flash window) → `_syncTicker()` sees `region.hasLive == false` and disarms → nothing ever calls `setSubagentBoard` again (grep: the coordinator's `_push` is the only caller; there is no flash-end timer). Result:

- a **lone** settled agent stays **bright forever** (the common single-subagent case);
- with other live rows it stays bright until an unrelated text change (a minute-flip of someone's age, a new spawn) happens to re-push — up to ~60 s late.

The region logic itself is correct (`UT-3` asserts the `bright` transition and passes) — the wiring just never ships the second render. The wiring test actually pins the broken behavior: it asserts the ticker disarms on settle and never checks that the dim state lands.

Fix (small):
1. Include brightness in the dedupe key, e.g. `[for (final r in rows) '${r.text}|${r.bright}']`.
2. Keep the ticker armed while a row is flashing — `want = _wired && (region.hasLive || region.hasFlashing)` (add a `hasFlashing`/`needsRepaint(now)` probe to `TaskBoardRegion`) — or schedule a one-shot `Timer(settleFlash)` on settle.

Then add a coordinator-level test asserting that a manual clock advance past `settleFlash` + `subagentBoardTickForTest()` produces a push with `bright=false`.

Comment 1 (BLOCKING — flash/dim):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the settle flash never collapses to dim in the pushed TUI**

`_push()` dedupes on TEXT only, and the 1 Hz ticker disarms as soon as no row is live — so the `bright=false` render at flash end (3 s after settle, `TaskBoardRegion.rows`) is never delivered. Verified flow: settle event → `refresh()` pushes `bright=true` rows → `_syncTicker()` disarms (`region.hasLive` false) → no later push carries the dim flag. A lone settled agent therefore stays BRIGHT forever; with other live rows it stays bright up to a minute until an unrelated text change re-pushes. This is delta 9 / AC3's "3 s flash then dim one-liner" — the region logic is right (UT-3 passes) but the wiring never ships the second render.

Fix: make the dedupe key include brightness (e.g. `'${row.text}|${row.bright}'`) and keep the ticker armed while any row is flashing (`region.hasLive || region.hasFlashing(now)`), or schedule a one-shot `Timer(settleFlash)` on settle. Add a coordinator-level test asserting the post-flash push lands with `bright=false` (the current test pins the disarm and never checks the dim delivery).

Comment 2 (BLOCKING — width overflow):

🚨 **BLOCKING: age/cost fields overflow their fixed 4 cells — rows exceed the width budget (AC1)**

`subagentAgeLabel` renders `1h30m` (5 cells) for every agent ≥ 1 h (`12h34m` = 6) although its own contract (lines 212-214) promises ≤ 4 cells (`2h15`). Same for `subagentCompactTokens`: `12.3k` (5 cells) for 10,000-99,949 tokens not round multiples of 1000, and `12.3m` in the 10m-99.9m band. Reproduced: a 1h30m/12.3k record with an 80-char preview renders a 102-cell row at width 100 → AC1 broken, and the age/cost/preview columns start at different cells per row whenever ages/costs straddle the boundary (delta 6's fixed rail). The painter's `_clipToWidth` belt hides the wrap but not the misalignment (and eats preview cells).

Fix: drop the trailing `m` in the hours branch → `2h15`; in both compact bands keep one decimal only below 10 (`4.1k`, `9.9m`) and switch to integer units at ≥10 (`12k`, `12m`). Add matrix cases at ≥1h and 10k+/10m+ non-round costs — the current matrix pins `at(0)`, so it can't see this.

Comment 3 (SUGGESTION — ANSI strip):

💡 **SUGGESTION: strip control/ANSI sequences from the preview**

The preview flattens newlines but passes ANSI escape sequences through; they measure zero-width (`tuiTextWidth` classifies 0x00-0x1f as zero-width) so `tuiFitWidth` keeps them and the row writes them into the frame. The model-authored task string is the same trust domain as chat text (which renders raw too), so this is hardening, not a hole — but since the board pre-renders host-side, `stripAnsi(previewSource)` (already exported by `tui_repl.dart`) is a one-call guarantee that the row stays plain text.

Comment 4 (SUGGESTION — squeeze yield order):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `_visibleSubagentRows` doesn't implement "settled summaries yield first"**

`rows.sublist(rows.length - plan.subagents)` keeps the NEWEST rows under squeeze. Newest ≈ live in the common case, but a long-lived child that spawned before later, already-settled siblings is dropped while dim summaries persist — exactly what the comment above ("settled summaries yield first") and the PR description promise against. Sort before slicing: live rows first (oldest-first), then settled newest-first, take `plan.subagents`.

The reason is legitimate (the status row legitimately paints `run scout#1` in the chat view), but wait — let me think about this. The hub overlay guard test verifies that overlay content doesn't leak into the chat view. The new status row legitimately shows the subagent name in the chat view — that's by design (gh-1415). So the test needed to anchor on the full tree row form. That's reasonable, though weakening the assertion from name → name (type) does reduce the guard's sensitivity. The new subagent board shows the name so it's not a leak. OK.

Now the key files to review:
1. `subagent_board.dart` — reviewed above. Potential issues:
   - `subagentRecordOf` — previewSource uses `task ?? handle.task`. Check `SubagentHandle` for the `task` field.
   - `subagentAgeLabel`: `2h15` format — `'${hours}h${(minutes % 60).toString().padLeft(2, '0')}m'` — wait, `2h15m` is 5 cells > 4! Let me check: hours=2, minutes%60=15 → "2h15m" — that's 5 characters. The doc comment says "Fixed ≤ 4 cells: `42s`, `12m`, `2h15`, capped at `99h+`" — but the code produces `2h15m` (5 cells), not `2h15` (4 cells). Hmm — wait let me re-read:

```dart
  return '${hours}h${(minutes % 60).toString().padLeft(2, '0')}m';
```

For 2h15m → `2h15m` — that's 5 chars. The doc says ≤ 4 cells and gives example `2h15`. So the code contradicts the doc comment. Also `10h05m` = 6 cells! And since `age` is `padLeft(_ageCells)` = padLeft(4), a 5-6 cell value would break the fixed width and reflow the row (misaligning neighbors). Actually the age field is just joined into head: `'$glyph $state $name $age $cost'` — if age is 5-6 cells, head grows and the total width computation may overflow `w`. Let me check: `nameBudget = (w - (_railFloorCells - 1)).clamp(1, _nameCells)` and `previewBudget = w - _railFloorCells - nameBudget`. If w = 100: railFloor = 2+1+4+1+1+1+4+1+4 = let me compute: `_glyphZoneCells + 1 + _stateCells + 1 + 1 + 1 + _ageCells + 1 + _costCells` = 2+1+4+1+1+1+4+1+4 = 19. nameBudget = (100 - 18).clamp(1,16) = 16. previewBudget = 100 - 19 - 16 = 65. head = 2 +1+ 4 +1+ 16 +1+ 4 +1+ 4 = 34 cells; head + 1 + 65 = 100. OK.

But if age renders 5-6 cells (e.g. `2h15m`), head = 35-36 and total = 101-102 > width → line wraps or overflows the budget. The TUI painter clips `_clipToWidth(boardRow.text)` — so the preview would get clipped, but the row's own fixed-rail would be misaligned vs other rows (age column not fixed width). Minor issue but a real bug vs its own spec ("Fixed ≤ 4 cells", "digit growth never reflows the row"). Also `padLeft(4)` on `99h+` (4 cells) is fine. So the bug: hours < 60 & minutes%60 → `XhYYm` is 5+ cells for hours 1-99 (e.g. `1h05m` = 5 cells, `12h34m` = 6 cells). Doc comment says the format is `2h15`. So there's an inconsistency — the trailing `m` makes it 5 cells minimum for hours≥1. This is a genuine bug (BLOCKING? It's a display misalignment for agents running ≥1h; the row exceeds width → wrap/clip). Severity: the code contradicts its own documented invariant (AC1: exactly ONE line ≤ 100 columns; E1: fixed rail). For a row at width 100 with a long preview, the extra 2 cells push the line to 102 > 100 → wrap (violates "never wrap"). I'd class as BLOCKING? Hmm. Let me think — is it a "broken behavior" bug? For subagents running over an hour, rows misalign and can wrap. The card's whole point is alignment/density. It's an edge (age ≥ 1h subagent) but the pin facts mention 12m/41k in the example. The unit tests presumably test `2h15m`? Let me check the test file to see what golden strings they assert.

Let me also verify the claimed AC1 "≤ 100 columns" test.

2. `TaskBoardRegion.upsert`: `existing.settledAt = null` for non-terminal — resume revives the row. But wait: if a child is re-spawned... ids are unique so unlikely.

Interesting: in `upsert`, `_pruneSettled()` is only called on the existing-row path — not when a new row is inserted (inserts are non-terminal, so no pruning needed... actually pruning settled rows only matters when count > cap, and a new insert can't add a settled row. Fine).

But there's a subtle issue: `rows()` dedups names across the VISIBLE set — comment says "a folded row cannot force a suffix on a visible one" — the code counts `_rows.values` which IS the visible set (folded rows are removed). OK consistent.

3. Coordinator: `refresh()` iterates `handles` and upserts each. But rows for subagents that are removed from the registry: `handles` — does the registry retain completed subagents forever (retained subagents)? The description says "retained `SubagentHandle` registry". If a handle is removed from the registry (e.g. after abort/retire), the region row would remain forever (region never removes rows except via `_pruneSettled` cap and `clear()`). Terminal rows persist until 4-cap fold. That's per spec (persist one line, fold on pressure). But a row whose handle is evicted would keep ticking? No — terminal rows don't tick (`hasLive` only live rows). But their age would freeze? Age keeps recomputing from spawnedAt — wait, `rows(now:)` recomputes age for terminal rows too! So a settled row's age keeps growing every render... but the coordinator's `_push` dedupe only pushes when text changes — the age of a settled row changes only when the minute flips (minute granularity). So a done row's age ticks up indefinitely (12m → 13m...) — is that intended? The spec says the row collapses to a one-liner summary; an age that keeps ticking on a done row is arguably fine (age of the agent lifetime) — omp keeps elapsed time. Hmm, but the ticker: `_syncTicker` arms only while `region.hasLive` — if ONLY settled rows remain, ticker is disarmed, and the pushed frame's age becomes stale until the next registry event/refresh. That's fine-ish.

Actually wait — there's a subtle dedupe issue: after the last live row settles, the flash period is 3s. The flash (bright → dim) changes rendering but the TEXT stays the same (bright flag changes only). `_push` dedupes on TEXT ONLY: `texts`. So the bright→dim transition at the end of the flash is only pushed if a text change happens simultaneously. Let me trace: coordinator `_push()` computes rows with `bright` flags; dedupe on texts; if texts unchanged, no push. So after a settle at t0: refresh() pushes rows with bright=true (inside flash). During flash: ticker? After settle, `hasLive` — if other rows are live, ticker keeps running; each tick `_push()` — texts unchanged (age minute-granularity may change) — if no text change, no push. At t0+3s the flash ends: bright=false — but texts unchanged → NO PUSH → the row stays bright forever until some text change. That's a real bug: the settle flash never visually collapses to dim unless coincident text change. Hmm wait — but when the last live row settles, does the ticker stop? `_syncTicker` is called in `refresh()` and `_tick()`. Sequence: settle event → registry event → refresh() → upsert (settles row) → _push() (bright, flash) → _syncTicker() (hasLive false → disarm). So ticker disarmed at settle. Flash end at +3s: nothing re-renders → row remains bright indefinitely. The PTY E2E asserts `done\s+boardwatch` appears — it would pass even if bright. And the dimness is a `bright` flag — visual only. So the "3s flash then dim" spec (delta 9: collapse to dim one-liner) is broken in the common case (no further events). 

Hold on — let me double-check `_visibleSubagentRows`/`_writeSubagentBoard`: dim rows render `_dim(text)`. Bright rows plain. The dim transition requires a new SubagentBoardMsg with bright=false. The only way: `_push()` called again with same texts → dedupe blocks. Unless... `region.rows()` is called from elsewhere? `subagentBoardRowsForTest` only. So yes — the flash-to-dim collapse never repaints. Wait, but is there any timer that fires a push at flash end? Let me search for `settleFlash` usage in coordinator... The coordinator has `_ticker` 1 Hz, `_tick` only pushes while `hasLive`. `_syncTicker` wants `_wired && region.hasLive`. After ALL rows settle: …

Comment 1 (BLOCKING — flash/dim):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the settle flash never collapses to dim in the pushed TUI**

`_push()` dedupes on TEXT only, and the 1 Hz ticker disarms as soon as no row is live — so the `bright=false` render at flash end (3 s after settle, `TaskBoardRegion.rows`) is never delivered. Verified flow: settle event → `refresh()` pushes `bright=true` rows → `_syncTicker()` disarms (`region.hasLive` false) → no later push carries the dim flag. A lone settled agent therefore stays BRIGHT forever; with other live rows it stays bright up to a minute until an unrelated text change re-pushes. This is delta 9 / AC3's "3 s flash then dim one-liner" — the region logic is right (UT-3 passes) but the wiring never ships the second render.

Fix: make the dedupe key include brightness (e.g. `'${row.text}|${row.bright}'`) and keep the ticker armed while any row is flashing (`region.hasLive || region.hasFlashing(now)`), or schedule a one-shot `Timer(settleFlash)` on settle. Add a coordinator-level test asserting the post-flash push lands with `bright=false` (the current test pins the disarm and never checks the dim delivery).

Comment 2 (BLOCKING — width overflow):

🚨 **BLOCKING: age/cost fields overflow their fixed 4 cells — rows exceed the width budget (AC1)**

`subagentAgeLabel` renders `1h30m` (5 cells) for every agent ≥ 1 h (`12h34m` = 6) although its own contract (lines 212-214) promises ≤ 4 cells (`2h15`). Same for `subagentCompactTokens`: `12.3k` (5 cells) for 10,000-99,949 tokens not round multiples of 1000, and `12.3m` in the 10m-99.9m band. Reproduced: a 1h30m/12.3k record with an 80-char preview renders a 102-cell row at width 100 → AC1 broken, and the age/cost/preview columns start at different cells per row whenever ages/costs straddle the boundary (delta 6's fixed rail). The painter's `_clipToWidth` belt hides the wrap but not the misalignment (and eats preview cells).

Fix: drop the trailing `m` in the hours branch → `2h15`; in both compact bands keep one decimal only below 10 (`4.1k`, `9.9m`) and switch to integer units at ≥10 (`12k`, `12m`). Add matrix cases at ≥1h and 10k+/10m+ non-round costs — the current matrix pins `at(0)`, so it can't see this.

Comment 3 (SUGGESTION — ANSI strip):

💡 **SUGGESTION: strip control/ANSI sequences from the preview**

The preview flattens newlines but passes ANSI escape sequences through; they measure zero-width (`tuiTextWidth` classifies 0x00-0x1f as zero-width) so `tuiFitWidth` keeps them and the row writes them into the frame. The model-authored task string is the same trust domain as chat text (which renders raw too), so this is hardening, not a hole — but since the board pre-renders host-side, `stripAnsi(previewSource)` (already exported by `tui_repl.dart`) is a one-call guarantee that the row stays plain text.

Comment 4 (SUGGESTION — squeeze yield order):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `_visibleSubagentRows` doesn't implement "settled summaries yield first"**

`rows.sublist(rows.length - plan.subagents)` keeps the NEWEST rows under squeeze. Newest ≈ live in the common case, but a long-lived child that spawned before later, already-settled siblings is dropped while dim summaries persist — exactly what the comment above ("settled summaries yield first") and the PR description promise against. Sort before slicing: live rows first (oldest-first), then settled newest-first, take `plan.subagents`.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the settle flash never collapses to dim in the pushed TUI (delta 9 / AC3)**

`_push()` dedupes on **text only**, and the 1 Hz ticker disarms as soon as no row is live — so the post-flash render (`bright=false`, 3 s after settle) is never delivered to the TUI.

Flow: settle event → `refresh()` → `upsert` stamps `settledAt` → `_push()` ships rows with `bright=true` (inside the flash window) → `_syncTicker()` sees `region.hasLive == false` and disarms → nothing ever calls `setSubagentBoard` again (grep: the coordinator's `_push` is the only caller; there is no flash-end timer). Result:

- a **lone** settled agent stays **bright forever** (the common single-subagent case);
- with other live rows it stays bright until an unrelated text change (a minute-flip of someone's age, a new spawn) happens to re-push — up to ~60 s late.

The region logic itself is correct (`UT-3` asserts the `bright` transition and passes) — the wiring just never ships the second render. The wiring test actually pins the broken behavior: it asserts the ticker disarms on settle and never checks that the dim state lands.

Fix (small):
1. Include brightness in the dedupe key, e.g. `[for (final r in rows) '${r.text}|${r.bright}']`.
2. Keep the ticker armed while a row is flashing — `want = _wired && (region.hasLive || region.hasFlashing)` (add a `hasFlashing`/`needsRepaint(now)` probe to `TaskBoardRegion`) — or schedule a one-shot `Timer(settleFlash)` on settle.

Then add a coordinator-level test asserting that a manual clock advance past `settleFlash` + `subagentBoardTickForTest()` produces a push with `bright=false`.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: age/cost fields overflow their fixed 4-cell budgets — rows exceed the width budget (AC1, delta 6)**

`subagentAgeLabel` returns `'${hours}h${mm}m'` → **5–6 cells** for every agent ≥ 1 h (`1h30m`, `12h34m`) although its own doc contract three lines up promises "Fixed ≤ 4 cells: `42s`, `12m`, `2h15`". Same class of bug in `subagentCompactTokens`: the `< 100000` band emits one decimal for any k ≥ 10 → `12.3k` (5 cells) for 10,000–99,949 tokens that aren't round multiples of 1000, and the `< 100000000` band does the same → `12.3m`.

Reproduced against this tree (`dart run`):

```
age 5400s  -> "1h30m"  cells=5     cost 12345 -> "12.3k" cells=5
row cells=102 (budget 100)
```

Consequences: AC1 ("exactly ONE line ≤ width") is violated for any record ≥ 1 h old with a near-budget preview, and the fixed left rail misaligns — the age/cost/preview columns start at different cells per row whenever neighbors straddle the 1 h or 10k/10m boundary. The painter's `_clipToWidth` belt prevents an actual wrap but not the misalignment (and silently eats preview cells). Long-lived watcher agents — the card's own omp reference shows `12m`-class rows — hit this deterministically.

Fix:
- hours branch: drop the trailing `m` → `'${hours}h${(minutes % 60).toString().padLeft(2, '0')}'` (`2h15`, ≤ 4 cells; `99h+` unchanged).
- cost bands: keep one decimal only below 10 (`4.1k`, `9.9m`), integer units at ≥ 10 (`12k`, `12m`).

Coverage gap: the width matrix pins `at(0)` (age `0s`) and the goldens use `12m`/`41k`, so nothing exercises ≥ 1 h or non-round ≥ 10k/10m — add those cases and they fail on the current code.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: strip control/ANSI sequences from the preview**

The preview flattens newlines but passes ANSI escape sequences through untouched. They measure as zero-width (`tuiTextWidth` classifies 0x00–0x1f as zero-width), so `tuiFitWidth` keeps them and the raw bytes ride the pre-rendered row into the frame buffer.

The source is the model-authored `task` string — the same trust domain as chat text, which this TUI also renders un-sanitized — so this is hardening rather than an exploitable hole. But unlike the transcript, the board pre-renders host-side, where staying plain-text is a one-call guarantee:

```dart
final previewSource = stripAnsi((task ?? handle.task).replaceAll('\n', ' ').trim());
```

(`stripAnsi` is already exported by `tui_repl.dart`.)

💡 **SUGGESTION: the code doesn't implement the "settled summaries yield first" invariant its own comment states**

`rows.sublist(rows.length - plan.subagents)` keeps the **newest** rows under squeeze. Newest ≈ live in the common case (settled rows are usually older spawns), but the ordering is not guaranteed: a long-lived child that spawned *before* later, already-settled siblings is dropped while dim one-line summaries persist — exactly what the comment above ("live rows stay visible, settled summaries yield first") and the PR description promise against.

Cheap fix — sort before slicing:

```dart
final ranked = [
  ...rows.where((r) => r.bright),            // live first, spawn order
  ...rows.where((r) => !r.bright).reversed,  // settled newest-first
];
return ranked.take(plan.subagents).toList();
```

(Ranking on `bright` keeps it aligned with the flash semantics; purely visual either way — it self-corrects as rows settle/fold — hence suggestion level.)

Comment 1 (BLOCKING — flash/dim):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the settle flash never collapses to dim in the pushed TUI**

`_push()` dedupes on TEXT only, and the 1 Hz ticker disarms as soon as no row is live — so the `bright=false` render at flash end (3 s after settle, `TaskBoardRegion.rows`) is never delivered. Verified flow: settle event → `refresh()` pushes `bright=true` rows → `_syncTicker()` disarms (`region.hasLive` false) → no later push carries the dim flag. A lone settled agent therefore stays BRIGHT forever; with other live rows it stays bright up to a minute until an unrelated text change re-pushes. This is delta 9 / AC3's "3 s flash then dim one-liner" — the region logic is right (UT-3 passes) but the wiring never ships the second render.

Fix: make the dedupe key include brightness (e.g. `'${row.text}|${row.bright}'`) and keep the ticker armed while any row is flashing (`region.hasLive || region.hasFlashing(now)`), or schedule a one-shot `Timer(settleFlash)` on settle. Add a coordinator-level test asserting the post-flash push lands with `bright=false` (the current test pins the disarm and never checks the dim delivery).

Comment 2 (BLOCKING — width overflow):

🚨 **BLOCKING: age/cost fields overflow their fixed 4 cells — rows exceed the width budget (AC1)**

`subagentAgeLabel` renders `1h30m` (5 cells) for every agent ≥ 1 h (`12h34m` = 6) although its own contract (lines 212-214) promises ≤ 4 cells (`2h15`). Same for `subagentCompactTokens`: `12.3k` (5 cells) for 10,000-99,949 tokens not round multiples of 1000, and `12.3m` in the 10m-99.9m band. Reproduced: a 1h30m/12.3k record with an 80-char preview renders a 102-cell row at width 100 → AC1 broken, and the age/cost/preview columns start at different cells per row whenever ages/costs straddle the boundary (delta 6's fixed rail). The painter's `_clipToWidth` belt hides the wrap but not the misalignment (and eats preview cells).

Fix: drop the trailing `m` in the hours branch → `2h15`; in both compact bands keep one decimal only below 10 (`4.1k`, `9.9m`) and switch to integer units at ≥10 (`12k`, `12m`). Add matrix cases at ≥1h and 10k+/10m+ non-round costs — the current matrix pins `at(0)`, so it can't see this.

Comment 3 (SUGGESTION — ANSI strip):

💡 **SUGGESTION: strip control/ANSI sequences from the preview**

The preview flattens newlines but passes ANSI escape sequences through; they measure zero-width (`tuiTextWidth` classifies 0x00-0x1f as zero-width) so `tuiFitWidth` keeps them and the row writes them into the frame. The model-authored task string is the same trust domain as chat text (which renders raw too), so this is hardening, not a hole — but since the board pre-renders host-side, `stripAnsi(previewSource)` (already exported by `tui_repl.dart`) is a one-call guarantee that the row stays plain text.

Comment 4 (SUGGESTION — squeeze yield order):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `_visibleSubagentRows` doesn't implement "settled summaries yield first"**

`rows.sublist(rows.length - plan.subagents)` keeps the NEWEST rows under squeeze. Newest ≈ live in the common case, but a long-lived child that spawned before later, already-settled siblings is dropped while dim summaries persist — exactly what the comment above ("settled summaries yield first") and the PR description promise against. Sort before slicing: live rows first (oldest-first), then settled newest-first, take `plan.subagents`.

Comment 1 (BLOCKING — flash/dim):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the settle flash never collapses to dim in the pushed TUI**

`_push()` dedupes on TEXT only, and the 1 Hz ticker disarms as soon as no row is live — so the `bright=false` render at flash end (3 s after settle, `TaskBoardRegion.rows`) is never delivered. Verified flow: settle event → `refresh()` pushes `bright=true` rows → `_syncTicker()` disarms (`region.hasLive` false) → no later push carries the dim flag. A lone settled agent therefore stays BRIGHT forever; with other live rows it stays bright up to a minute until an unrelated text change re-pushes. This is delta 9 / AC3's "3 s flash then dim one-liner" — the region logic is right (UT-3 passes) but the wiring never ships the second render.

Fix: make the dedupe key include brightness (e.g. `'${row.text}|${row.bright}'`) and keep the ticker armed while any row is flashing (`region.hasLive || region.hasFlashing(now)`), or schedule a one-shot `Timer(settleFlash)` on settle. Add a coordinator-level test asserting the post-flash push lands with `bright=false` (the current test pins the disarm and never checks the dim delivery).

Comment 2 (BLOCKING — width overflow):

🚨 **BLOCKING: age/cost fields overflow their fixed 4 cells — rows exceed the width budget (AC1)**

`subagentAgeLabel` renders `1h30m` (5 cells) for every agent ≥ 1 h (`12h34m` = 6) although its own contract (lines 212-214) promises ≤ 4 cells (`2h15`). Same for `subagentCompactTokens`: `12.3k` (5 cells) for 10,000-99,949 tokens not round multiples of 1000, and `12.3m` in the 10m-99.9m band. Reproduced: a 1h30m/12.3k record with an 80-char preview renders a 102-cell row at width 100 → AC1 broken, and the age/cost/preview columns start at different cells per row whenever ages/costs straddle the boundary (delta 6's fixed rail). The painter's `_clipToWidth` belt hides the wrap but not the misalignment (and eats preview cells).

Fix: drop the trailing `m` in the hours branch → `2h15`; in both compact bands keep one decimal only below 10 (`4.1k`, `9.9m`) and switch to integer units at ≥10 (`12k`, `12m`). Add matrix cases at ≥1h and 10k+/10m+ non-round costs — the current matrix pins `at(0)`, so it can't see this.

Comment 3 (SUGGESTION — ANSI strip):

💡 **SUGGESTION: strip control/ANSI sequences from the preview**

The preview flattens newlines but passes ANSI escape sequences through; they measure zero-width (`tuiTextWidth` classifies 0x00-0x1f as zero-width) so `tuiFitWidth` keeps them and the row writes them into the frame. The model-authored task string is the same trust domain as chat text (which renders raw too), so this is hardening, not a hole — but since the board pre-renders host-side, `stripAnsi(previewSource)` (already exported by `tui_repl.dart`) is a one-call guarantee that the row stays plain text.

Comment 4 (SUGGESTION — squeeze yield order):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `_visibleSubagentRows` doesn't implement "settled summaries yield first"**

`rows.sublist(rows.length - plan.subagents)` keeps the NEWEST rows under squeeze. Newest ≈ live in the common case, but a long-lived child that spawned before later, already-settled siblings is dropped while dim summaries persist — exactly what the comment above ("settled summaries yield first") and the PR description promise against. Sort before slicing: live rows first (oldest-first), then settled newest-first, take `plan.subagents`.

Comment 1 (BLOCKING — flash/dim):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the settle flash never collapses to dim in the pushed TUI**

`_push()` dedupes on TEXT only, and the 1 Hz ticker disarms as soon as no row is live — so the `bright=false` render at flash end (3 s after settle, `TaskBoardRegion.rows`) is never delivered. Verified flow: settle event → `refresh()` pushes `bright=true` rows → `_syncTicker()` disarms (`region.hasLive` false) → no later push carries the dim flag. A lone settled agent therefore stays BRIGHT forever; with other live rows it stays bright up to a minute until an unrelated text change re-pushes. This is delta 9 / AC3's "3 s flash then dim one-liner" — the region logic is right (UT-3 passes) but the wiring never ships the second render.

Fix: make the dedupe key include brightness (e.g. `'${row.text}|${row.bright}'`) and keep the ticker armed while any row is flashing (`region.hasLive || region.hasFlashing(now)`), or schedule a one-shot `Timer(settleFlash)` on settle. Add a coordinator-level test asserting the post-flash push lands with `bright=false` (the current test pins the disarm and never checks the dim delivery).

Comment 2 (BLOCKING — width overflow):

🚨 **BLOCKING: age/cost fields overflow their fixed 4 cells — rows exceed the width budget (AC1)**

`subagentAgeLabel` renders `1h30m` (5 cells) for every agent ≥ 1 h (`12h34m` = 6) although its own contract (lines 212-214) promises ≤ 4 cells (`2h15`). Same for `subagentCompactTokens`: `12.3k` (5 cells) for 10,000-99,949 tokens not round multiples of 1000, and `12.3m` in the 10m-99.9m band. Reproduced: a 1h30m/12.3k record with an 80-char preview renders a 102-cell row at width 100 → AC1 broken, and the age/cost/preview columns start at different cells per row whenever ages/costs straddle the boundary (delta 6's fixed rail). The painter's `_clipToWidth` belt hides the wrap but not the misalignment (and eats preview cells).

Fix: drop the trailing `m` in the hours branch → `2h15`; in both compact bands keep one decimal only below 10 (`4.1k`, `9.9m`) and switch to integer units at ≥10 (`12k`, `12m`). Add matrix cases at ≥1h and 10k+/10m+ non-round costs — the current matrix pins `at(0)`, so it can't see this.

Comment 3 (SUGGESTION — ANSI strip):

💡 **SUGGESTION: strip control/ANSI sequences from the preview**

The preview flattens newlines but passes ANSI escape sequences through; they measure zero-width (`tuiTextWidth` classifies 0x00-0x1f as zero-width) so `tuiFitWidth` keeps them and the row writes them into the frame. The model-authored task string is the same trust domain as chat text (which renders raw too), so this is hardening, not a hole — but since the board pre-renders host-side, `stripAnsi(previewSource)` (already exported by `tui_repl.dart`) is a one-call guarantee that the row stays plain text.

Comment 4 (SUGGESTION — squeeze yield order):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `_visibleSubagentRows` doesn't implement "settled summaries yield first"**

`rows.sublist(rows.length - plan.subagents)` keeps the NEWEST rows under squeeze. Newest ≈ live in the common case, but a long-lived child that spawned before later, already-settled siblings is dropped while dim summaries persist — exactly what the comment above ("settled summaries yield first") and the PR description promise against. Sort before slicing: live rows first (oldest-first), then settled newest-first, take `plan.subagents`.

Verified flow: settle event → `refresh()` pushes `bright=true` rows → `_syncTicker()` disarms (`region.hasLive` false) → no later push carries the dim flag.
